tools.name: save_scene
tools.description: Resave a scene FILE via a separate headless Godot process, entirely independent of any running editor: it load()s the .tscn fresh from disk, instantiates it, and re-packs THAT — it never sees the live editor's in-memory scene state. If a bridge tool (add_node_live, set_property, set_transform, ...) has changed the live scene since the last save, those changes are NOT on disk yet and this tool will silently discard them while still reporting success. Confirmed live (2026-09-22): a real session hit exactly this. Use save_scene_live instead whenever an editor is open for this project — this file-based tool is only correct for scenes whose only edits came through file-based tools (create_scene, add_node) with no live editor session involved.

tools.name: eval_expression
tools.description: Evaluate an arbitrary GDScript expression against a node in the live scene tree, running in the Godot editor, and return the result. Use this for anything the structured tools don't cover. The expression runs with the target node as `self`, and also has direct access to ProjectSettings, ClassDB, Engine, Input, OS, Time, Performance, AudioServer, ResourceLoader (e.g. ResourceLoader.load("res://...") — plain load() is not available), ResourceSaver, and (in-editor) EditorInterface, e.g. "AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(AudioServer.get_bus_index(\"Music\"), -6.0)". Also has KEY_* constants (e.g. "Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_A)") — these are ordinary GDScript globals elsewhere, but Expression doesn't resolve them unless explicitly bound like this. Note: Expression syntax cannot parse assignment statements or loops — for those, use a structured tool. "Invalid named index 'x' for base type Object" means `.x` was read from a null (a find_child/get_node that found nothing, or an unset property), or x isn't in scope. Values are Godot's var_to_str() string encoding (e.g. "5", "true", "\"hello\"", "Vector2(1, 2)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"; colours may also be "#ff0000") — not plain JSON.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

expression.description: GDScript expression to evaluate, e.g. "position.x" or "$Sprite2D.modulate"

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Run multi-statement GDScript source against a node in the live scene tree, running in the Godot editor. Use this instead of eval_expression whenever the logic needs a `var` declaration, a loop, or more than one statement — Expression (what eval_expression uses) can only parse a single expression. `source` becomes the body of a compiled `func _run(node):`, so it can reference the target node as `node` (not `self`) and MUST end with its own `return` statement — unlike eval_expression, there is no implicit return of a trailing expression. Also has access to ProjectSettings, ClassDB, Engine, Input, OS, Time, Performance, AudioServer, ResourceLoader (e.g. ResourceLoader.load("res://...") — plain load() is not available), ResourceSaver, and (in-editor) EditorInterface as bare identifiers. Note: a runtime error partway through the script (as opposed to a compile error) is not caught — you get back null; check get_debug_output for what actually went wrong. Values are Godot's var_to_str() string encoding (e.g. "5", "true", "\"hello\"", "Vector2(1, 2)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"; colours may also be "#ff0000") — not plain JSON.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

source.description:
GDScript statements forming a function body, e.g. "var root = EditorInterface.get_edited_scene_root()
var total = 0
for c in root.get_children():
	total += 1
return total"

tools.name: get_node_properties
tools.description: Get the editor-visible properties of one or more live nodes and their current values. For a Node2D/Node3D, position/rotation/scale here are LOCAL (relative to the parent) — global_position/global_rotation/global_transform (world-space, what matters most under nested parents) are also included even though Godot doesn't flag them editor-visible, since they're real settable properties too. To inspect several nodes (e.g. every control in a panel), pass node_paths in ONE call rather than one call per node, and pass properties to get just the values you need instead of every property of every node. Values are Godot's var_to_str() string encoding (e.g. "5", "true", "\"hello\"", "Vector2(1, 2)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"; colours may also be "#ff0000") — not plain JSON.

A value of the form "load:res://path/to/file" is resolved via load() instead of var_to_str() decoding — use this to assign an existing texture or other resource file, e.g. {"albedo_texture": "load:res://icon.svg"}. tools.name: edit_script_text
tools.description: Edit a GDScript (.gd) or shader (.gdshader) file the way a person would: opens it in Godot's script/shader editor and changes the text there as one undoable edit. Give either `text` (the whole new file) or `old_text` + `new_text` (replace one exact match in the current text, unsaved edits included — much cheaper for a small change; fails if old_text is missing or matches more than once). The tab is left unsaved — it reaches disk on Ctrl+S or when the scene is played — so there is no "reload from disk?" prompt. Use this instead of writing .gd/.gdshader files directly while the editor is open. A path that doesn't exist yet is created on disk (like the editor's New Script dialog); attach it with attach_script / set_shader_material.

new_text.description: what to replace old_text with (may be empty to delete it)

save.description: Also save the script/shader to disk (like Ctrl+S) and verify the file. Default false: the edit stays in the editor tab, marked (*). The result always says saved, editor_matches, disk_matches and, for GDScript, parse_error.

tools.name: start_tour
tools.description:
Start a guided tour: a chain of editor highlights, each with a step card, that advances BY ITSELF when the user completes each step (checked against real editor state). Use it — without asking first — when the user says "show me", "teach me", "guide me", "walk me through" or "I want to learn", or when the message says teach mode is on (the panel's Teach toggle). Only for a bare "how do I…" that could mean either, offer both in one short line ("I can do it, or walk you through it with a guided tour — which?") rather than an open question. Inspect the scene first and use the user's real node names. Unlike highlight_editor_control, outlines persist through unrelated edits. The whole tour is validated first and every problem is reported at once; pass dry_run to validate only. Replaces any running tour.

Tour: {format: "godot-live-tour/1", title, vars?: {name: node_path}, requires?: {scene_open?, node_exists?: [paths]}, stuck_after_sec? (default 90; 0 = off), steps: [{id?, text, why?, target?, done_when, show_me?}]}.
- why: one or two sentences on why this step matters; shown by the card's Why? button (works with no agent). Pressed again, Why? sends the question to the in-editor agent panel.
- show_me: actions the card's Show me button runs to do the step for the user (undoable). Derived automatically from done_when for node_selected, node_added (with class), node_removed/renamed/reparented, property_equals, property_class (new resource of that class, e.g. a BoxMesh), script_attached (with script), signal_connected (with method), in_group, scene_open, scene_saved, game_running, script_contains (creates/edits the script with your code, opens and saves it), property_changed (nudges the current value), control_pressed (presses the outlined button), manual (just moves on) and all. Show me announces what it is about to do, then does it; it refuses @tool scripts and anything under addons/. Give an explicit show_me only when the derived one wouldn't fit. Explicit form: [{command, ...bridge params}], command one of select_nodes, add_node_live, set_property, set_nested_property {node_path, property_path, value}, set_resource_property {node_path, property_name, resource_type}, rename_node, reparent_node, remove_node, connect_signal, set_node_groups, set_properties, set_transform, duplicate_node, add_mesh_instance, setup_collision, set_material_3d, set_physics_material, setup_environment, edit_script_text {path, text | old_text+new_text, save}, attach_script, save_scene_live, open_scene {path}, play_scene.
- script_contains {script | node_path, text, extends?, replace?}: the script's text contains text (whitespace ignored) — use it for "type this code" steps; Show me writes it (replace: the snippet text replaces; extends: base class for a new file).
- text: short instruction; **bold**, `code` and fenced ``` blocks are rendered. "$name" in text shows that var's CURRENT node name — refer to nodes this way ("Select **$ball**"), never by a typed-out name, so the card matches what the user called it.
- target: what to outline — node_path (its Scene dock row, WITHOUT selecting it), node_path + property (that Inspector row), or an editor control: root ("scene_tree", "inspector", "filesystem", "bottom_panel", "editor") + tooltip / text / class / index / path, plus an optional label. Icon-only buttons like the Scene dock's + have no text: use {"root": "scene_tree", "tooltip": "Add/Create a New Node"}. Omit target for a card-only step. If it can't be found the step still runs, with a note on the card.
- done_when ALWAYS has a "type" (state checks preferred): "node_selected" {node_path} | "node_exists" {node_path} | "node_added" {parent, class?, name?, capture?} (a new child since the step began; capture binds it to a var so later steps follow it whatever it is called; name is only a SUGGESTION: the step then asks the user to rename it, and completes once they give it any name of their own — later steps still work, whatever they chose — so give main objects a name from the request, e.g. "Ball") | "node_removed" {node_path} | "node_renamed" {node_path, name} | "node_reparented" {node_path, parent} | "property_equals" {node_path, property (sub-paths ok, e.g. "position:y"), value (var_to_str form, "load:res://…" or "#ff0000"), tolerance?} | "property_changed" {node_path, property} | "property_class" {node_path, property, class} (a new resource of that class, e.g. a BoxMesh) | "script_attached" {node_path, script?} | "script_contains" {script | node_path, text, extends?, replace?} (the script's text contains text, whitespace ignored — for "type this code" steps) | "script_ok" {script | node_path} (parses with no errors) | "output_contains" {text} (Output panel / game prints since the step began) | "no_errors" (no new errors since the step began) | "game_property" {node_path, property, op: > < >= <= == ~=, value} (a property in the RUNNING game) | "signal_connected" {source, signal, target, method?} | "in_group" {node_path, group} | "scene_open" {path} | "scene_saved" | "file_exists" {path} | "control_pressed" (the step's target button was pressed; fallback only) | "game_running" | "manual" (user clicks Next) | "all"/"any" {checks: [...]}.
- verify (optional, any step): a check that the result WORKED, run after done_when passes — use it after code steps (script_ok) and after running the game (output_contains, game_property, no_errors). On failure the card says what is wrong and get_tour_status shows a verify_failed event; the step completes by itself once the learner fixes it. wait_sec? sets how long it waits before reporting.
- on_fail (optional, with verify): {note?, steps?: [steps]} — if the verify fails, the card shows note and the steps are inserted as fix-up steps (once per step, no nesting); then the original step is checked again. Keep fix-ups short.
- skip_if (optional): a check; if already true when the step would start, the step is skipped without being shown.
- Anywhere a node path is accepted, "$name" or "$name/Child" refers to a var.
- The card gives the user Back, Skip, Why?, Show me and ✕; it shows a gentle hint when they do the wrong thing (wrong class, wrong parent, wrong value or name) and a "stuck?" note after stuck_after_sec.
Validation checks property and signal names against the real classes; editor controls that can't be found yet are warnings, not errors (they may appear later, e.g. in a dialog).
Example (note done_when always has a "type" field, and node paths are "$var" or relative to the scene root):
{"format": "godot-live-tour/1", "title": "A green floor", "requires": {"scene_open": "res://main.tscn"}, "vars": {"root": "."}, "steps": [{"text": "Click **+** and add a `StaticBody3D` under **$root**.", "why": "A static body is solid but never moves.", "target": {"root": "scene_tree", "tooltip": "Add/Create a New Node"}, "done_when": {"type": "node_added", "parent": "$root", "class": "StaticBody3D", "name": "Floor", "capture": "floor"}}, {"text": "Give **$floor** a `MeshInstance3D` child.", "target": {"root": "scene_tree", "tooltip": "Add/Create a New Node"}, "done_when": {"type": "node_added", "parent": "$floor", "class": "MeshInstance3D", "capture": "mesh"}}, {"text": "Set **$mesh**'s **Mesh** to a new **PlaneMesh**.", "target": {"node_path": "$mesh", "property": "mesh"}, "done_when": {"type": "property_class", "node_path": "$mesh", "property": "mesh", "class": "PlaneMesh"}}]}
Keep tours to 3–8 steps, one action each; prefer state checks over manual. Check progress with get_tour_status.

The card tells the learner the plan changed (show note). Use this INSTEAD of changing the scene yourself. Steps use the same format as start_tour; validated first, all problems at once; dry_run to check only. from_step may be the step after the current one (to keep the current step and change what follows).

tools.description: Search the OFFICIAL Godot Asset Library (godotengine.org/asset-library) for addons. When the user asks for an addon, plugin or tool for Godot, search here FIRST, before suggesting GitHub or the web. Results fit the open editor's Godot version and show title, author, license, support level (official / community / testing), rating, version and last update. Tell the user what you found and ask which to install, unless they already named one. The newer store.godotengine.org has no public API, so it is not searched.

query.description: What to search for, e.g. "dialogue", "state machine", "terrain"

godot_version.description: e.g. "4.7"; default: the open editor's version

tools.name: install_asset
tools.description: Install an Asset Library asset (the asset_id from search_assets) into the open project: downloads the exact published version from its official source, verifies the checksum when the library gives one, and extracts its addons/ folder into res://addons/. Never overwrites existing files unless overwrite is true, and does NOT enable the plugin — a plugin runs code inside the editor. Always tell the user the title, author and license first, and enable the plugin (Project > Project Settings > Plugins) only when they agree. Assets without an addons/ folder (templates, demos) need include: "all", which puts everything in res://<name>/.

include.description: addons (default): only the addons/ folder. all: everything, into res://<name>/

overwrite.description: Replace files that already exist (default false)

tools.name: get_perf_stats
tools.description: How much time the GodotLiveMCP addon itself spends in its periodic work, in ms: the per-frame bridge polling, running tours (tour_process per frame, tour_check each ~0.5 s), Watch (watch_process), and record mode (recorder_diff per change), plus the editor's frame rate and node count. Use it to check the addon is not slowing the editor: reset the probes, do the work you want to measure, then read them. Probes show calls, avg_ms, max_ms and last_ms.

reset.description: Clear the probes after reading (default false)

tools.name: get_tour_status
tools.description: Where the user is in the guided tour: current step, seconds on it, captured vars (as current node paths), and the problems (the recent things that went wrong on the current step: verify_failed, show_me_failed, wrong_action, stuck…), current_step, and the event log (step_started, step_done, already_done, wrong_action, stuck, target_missing, skipped, back_to_step, why_shown, why_asked, show_me, show_me_failed, stopped, tour_done), plus any note currently on the card (note_target / note_hint / note_stuck). Call this first when the user comes back to chat mid-tour.

tools.name: save_tour
tools.description: Save the running (or last) guided tour as a .tour.json file — default res://tours/<title>.tour.json — so it can be replayed later with NO agent: from Project > Tools > Guided Tours… in the editor, or start_tour {path}. Offer this after a tour went well. The user can also press Save on the tour's final card. Tours are plain data (no code), safe to share.

tools.name: start_recording
tools.description: Record mode: start capturing changes to the open scene (nodes added/removed/renamed/moved, properties edited in the Inspector or viewport, scripts, groups, signal connections, saves) to turn into a draft guided tour. The user does the task themselves; undone changes drop out, repeated edits of one property become one step. A red bar in the editor shows it is recording; the user can stop it there too. Finish with stop_recording.

tools.name: stop_recording
tools.description: Stop record mode and build the draft tour (returned, and saved to res://tours/<title>.tour.json unless save is false). Text, switches, dropdowns and new resources must match; numbers, vectors and colours only have to change unless exact is true (the step text shows the value used). Steps have no why text yet — offer to add plain-language why lines and better wording, then save the improved tour (edit the file, or start_tour + save_tour).

tools.name: get_recording_status
tools.description: Whether record mode is on, and the steps captured so far (one line each).

tools.name: set_watch_mode
tools.description: Turn Watch mode on or off in the editor. While on, each change you make through these tools is shown to the user as it happens: the node or property you touched is briefly outlined and a small log lists what you did ("added Ball (RigidBody3D)", "Ball · Mass → 2"). It never slows you down. Turn it on when the user says "let me watch", "show me what you're doing" or wants to follow along without doing it themselves (for "teach me", use a guided tour instead). The user can also toggle it with the panel's Watch button.

on.description: true to turn Watch on (default), false to turn it off

tools.name: list_tours
tools.description: List the saved .tour.json files in the project (path, title, step count, required scene).

tools.name: stop_tour
tools.description: End the running guided tour and remove its outlines and card.

tools.name: interact_control
tools.description: Operate an editor UI control found with dump_control_tree, to test a custom UI end to end without asking the user to click. Actions: press (buttons; toggles flip), set_value (SpinBox/sliders, CheckBox, OptionButton by index or text, LineEdit, TextEdit, ColorPickerButton), select_menu_item (MenuButton / OptionButton by id or item_text), drop_files (a FileSystem-dock drop of res:// paths onto a scripted control via its _can_drop_data/_drop_data), drag_drop (from one scripted control's _get_drag_data to another's _drop_data). Returns the control's state afterwards and `undo.added` — whether the editor's undo history gained an action. Identify the control by `path` (+ the same `root` as the dump), or by `text` and/or `class` (+ `index` if several match). Actions run through the control's signals/methods, not real mouse events, so native-only drag-and-drop (e.g. the Tree dock) is not covered.

root.description: Same root as the dump_control_tree call the path came from (default "inspector")

text.description: Match a visible control by its exact text instead of a path

class.description: Match by class (alone or with text), e.g. "Button"

index.description: Which match, when text/class matches several

value.description: set_value: number, boolean, string, option index/text, or a color string

at_position.description: drop_files: [x, y] inside the control (default its centre)

from.description: drag_drop: path of the control to drag from

to.description: drag_drop: path of the control to drop on

from_position.description: drag_drop: [x, y] inside the source (default centre)

to_position.description: drag_drop: [x, y] inside the target (default centre)

tools.name: refresh_editor_scripts
tools.description: Do the reload dance after edit_script_text on @tool scripts, addon plugins and resource scripts, in one call: saves the open scripts (edit_script_text leaves them unsaved, so the editor keeps running the old file on disk), re-parses them and returns the parse errors (a plugin enabled against a broken script silently does nothing), toggles the enabled addon plugin each script belongs to, re-selects the inspected object so the Inspector rebuilds, and lists typed members that read null on live nodes (a hot-reloaded script that gained a member leaves it unset on existing instances — set it with set_property). Superset of reload_plugin for this purpose. Without `paths`, refreshes every script open in the script editor.

paths.description: res:// script paths to refresh (default: all open scripts)

tools.name: get_editor_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the live editor's 3D viewport as a PNG image — the only way to get visual state, since nothing else exposes rendered pixels through get_node_properties or eval_expression. Returned as an image content block, not JSON.

max_dimension.description: Downscale so neither dimension exceeds this (default 800); pass 0 for full resolution

tools.name: setup_navigation
tools.description: Configure and bake a live NavigationRegion2D/3D's nav polygon/mesh in one call — creating the resource, applying properties, and baking are three separate steps otherwise, and baking specifically is a method call (bake_navigation_mesh()/bake_navigation_polygon()), unreachable through property tools. Bakes synchronously (blocks briefly) so the response reflects the finished result, rather than the default threaded bake this bridge has no way to await. Bakes from whatever geometry already exists under the region node in the scene, same as the editor's manual bake button. A value of the form "load:res://path/to/file" is resolved via load() instead of var_to_str() decoding — use this to assign an existing texture or other resource file, e.g. {"albedo_texture": "load:res://icon.svg"}. Nested colon-path property names like "material_override:albedo_texture" are NOT supported here — use set_nested_property for those instead. Unknown property names fail loudly rather than silently no-oping, and the response includes a readback of every value actually applied — trust that over assuming success from ok:true alone.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

nav_params.description: Properties to set on the NavigationMesh (3D) or NavigationPolygon (2D), var_to_str()-encoded, e.g. {"cell_size": "0.25"}

tools.name: get_resource_dependencies
tools.description: List a resource file's dependencies (other files it references) via ResourceLoader.get_dependencies() — a genuine capability gap, nothing else exposes a project's resource dependency graph. Useful before deleting or moving a file, to see what would break.

path.description: res:// path to the resource file, e.g. "res://level1.tscn"

tools.name: game_eval_expression
tools.description: Evaluate a GDScript expression against a node in a RUNNING GAME instance (not the editor) and return the result. The game-side counterpart to eval_expression. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor. Values are Godot's var_to_str() string encoding (e.g. "5", "true", "\"hello\"", "Vector2(1, 2)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"; colours may also be "#ff0000") — not plain JSON.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the running scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

expression.description: GDScript expression to evaluate, e.g. "position.x" or "health"

tools.name: game_list_scene_tree
tools.description: List the scene tree of a RUNNING GAME instance, starting at a node. The game-side counterpart to list_scene_tree. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the running scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

tools.name: game_get_node_properties
tools.description: Get all editor-visible properties (plus global transform for spatial nodes) of a node in a RUNNING GAME instance. The game-side counterpart to get_node_properties. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor. Values are Godot's var_to_str() string encoding (e.g. "5", "true", "\"hello\"", "Vector2(1, 2)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"; colours may also be "#ff0000") — not plain JSON.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the running scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

tools.name: game_set_property
tools.description: Set a property on a node in a RUNNING GAME instance. The game-side counterpart to set_property — no undo/redo at runtime, a direct assignment. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor. Values are Godot's var_to_str() string encoding (e.g. "5", "true", "\"hello\"", "Vector2(1, 2)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"; colours may also be "#ff0000") — not plain JSON.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the running scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

property_name.description: Name of the property to set

tools.name: game_set_properties
tools.description: Set multiple properties on a node in a RUNNING GAME instance in one call. The game-side counterpart to set_properties. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor. Values are Godot's var_to_str() string encoding (e.g. "5", "true", "\"hello\"", "Vector2(1, 2)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"; colours may also be "#ff0000") — not plain JSON.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the running scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

tools.name: get_game_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a RUNNING GAME instance's main viewport as a PNG image — actual gameplay, distinct from get_editor_screenshot which only sees the editor's 3D gizmo viewport. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor. Returned as an image content block, not JSON.

max_dimension.description: Downscale so neither dimension exceeds this (default 800); pass 0 for full resolution

tools.name: simulate_key
tools.description: Simulate a keyboard key press/release in a RUNNING GAME instance via Input.parse_input_event() — a real event fed into the engine's input pipeline (reaches _input()/_unhandled_input()/Input.is_action_pressed() the same way an actual keypress would), not just an internal flag flip. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor.

keycode.description: A single character (e.g. "a", "5", " ") or a special key name: "KEY_SPACE", "KEY_ENTER", "KEY_ESCAPE", "KEY_TAB", "KEY_BACKSPACE", "KEY_DELETE", "KEY_HOME", "KEY_END", "KEY_LEFT", "KEY_RIGHT", "KEY_UP", "KEY_DOWN", "KEY_SHIFT", "KEY_CTRL", "KEY_ALT", "KEY_F1".."KEY_F12"

pressed.description: true for key-down, false for key-up (default true)

tools.name: simulate_mouse_button
tools.description: Simulate a mouse button press/release at a viewport position in a RUNNING GAME instance. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor.

pressed.description: true for press, false for release (default true)

tools.name: simulate_mouse_motion
tools.description: Simulate mouse movement to a viewport position in a RUNNING GAME instance. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor.

tools.name: wait_for_game_condition
tools.description: Poll a boolean GDScript expression against a node in a RUNNING GAME instance once per frame until it's true or timeout_sec elapses (capped at 4s) — use this instead of repeatedly calling game_eval_expression in a loop yourself, which would be one bridge round trip per frame. Useful for assertions/tests that depend on game state settling over a few frames (e.g. waiting for a scene transition or an animation to finish) rather than a framework of dedicated assertion tools — reading state and judging pass/fail is something you can already do yourself with the read tools. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the running scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

timeout_sec.description: Max seconds to wait, capped at 4 (default 2)

tools.name: capture_game_frames
tools.description: Capture several screenshots of a RUNNING GAME spaced interval_sec apart (real time), returned as consecutive image blocks labelled with their timestamp — for judging motion, animation, or anything a single get_game_screenshot can't show. Total span (count-1)*interval_sec is capped at 10s. Pair with simulate_key etc. by sending the input first, then capturing. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor.

interval_sec.description: Seconds between frames (default 0.25; 0 = consecutive rendered frames)

max_dimension.description: Downscale so neither dimension exceeds this (default 400; 0 = full resolution)

tools.name: monitor_game_properties
tools.description: Sample node properties and/or expressions in a RUNNING GAME every interval_sec for duration_sec (max 10s) and return the time series as {columns, rows} — one call instead of polling game_eval_expression yourself. Use for "does the player actually fall / does health drain / does the velocity settle". Every watch entry is validated before sampling starts, so a misspelled property errors immediately. Values are Godot's var_to_str() string encoding (e.g. "5", "true", "\"hello\"", "Vector2(1, 2)", "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"; colours may also be "#ff0000") — not plain JSON. Requires runtime_bridge.gd to be added as a Project Settings > Autoload singleton in the target project, and the game to actually be running (e.g. via run_project) — this has no effect on the editor itself, only a live running game instance, a separate OS process from the editor.

watch.description: What to sample. Each entry: {node_path, property} or {node_path, expression}, plus optional label.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the running scene root (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"), or "." for the root

property.description: Property name; sub-paths like "position:y" or "velocity:x" are allowed

expression.description: GDScript expression evaluated with the node as self, e.g. "global_position.distance_to(get_node("../Goal").global_position)"

interval_sec.description: Seconds between samples (default 0.1; 0 = every rendered frame)

max_samples.description: Stop early after this many rows (default 200, max 1000)

tools.name: log_intent
tools.description: Log a short (one sentence) summary of what you're about to do, before making the tool calls for it. Call this once per conceptually distinct step — including each sub-step of a larger prompt that naturally decomposes into several — not once per trivial follow-up within the same step. This is what turns the shared usage log (see TOOL_CANDIDATES.md) from an undifferentiated pile of tool calls into reviewable {intent, calls, result} units. Pair with log_result once the step is done.

summary.description: One sentence: what is this step trying to accomplish, e.g. "add a bouncy platform to the scene"

tools.name: log_result
tools.description: Log a short outcome summary for the step most recently opened with log_intent, once its tool calls are done. The number of calls and errors made since that log_intent is recorded automatically — you don't need to count or report that yourself, just describe the outcome. The response includes pending_review_ready: true whenever a tool-candidate batch is waiting — mention this to the user when it comes up (e.g. "there's a tool-candidate batch ready whenever you want to look") rather than staying silent about it; a background server process has no other way to surface this.

summary.description: One sentence: what actually happened, e.g. "done, bounce=0.9 applied and verified" or "partial — moved but AI script wasn't attached"

tools.name: get_script_diagnostics
tools.description: Get real GDScript diagnostics (type errors, unused variables, and similar static checks) for a script, from Godot's own built-in language server — the same one VSCode's Godot extension uses. Requires the Godot editor to be open for this project (the LSP is part of the editor process). Checks on-disk content by default; pass `content` to check draft text instead, before it's ever written to disk — e.g. to validate a script before attach_script/run_script writes or runs it. Catches real static type errors (e.g. assigning a String to an int-typed variable) and warnings (e.g. unused variables), but is not exhaustive — it does not catch every possible mistake (e.g. calling a nonexistent method on a loosely-typed value may go unflagged); treat a clean result as "no issues found", not a full correctness guarantee.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the Godot project directory (same as other tools' projectPath)

scriptPath.description: res://-relative path to the script, e.g. "res://addons/godot_live_mcp/bridge.gd"

content.description: Optional: check this text instead of the file's current on-disk content (e.g. a draft not yet saved)
